overview: ECGC Export Credit Guarantee Schemes provide financial assistance to Indian exporters by offering credit guarantees against risks of non-payment by overseas buyers due to commercial or political reasons. The scheme supports export growth by mitigating payment risks and enhancing access to working capital finance from banks. It covers both pre-shipment and post-shipment stages of export transactions.
objectives: Provide credit guarantee covers to protect exporters against payment defaults by overseas buyers
Facilitate easier access to export finance from banks and financial institutions
Promote Indian exports by mitigating commercial and political risks
Support MSME exporters through tailored guarantee products
Enhance competitiveness of Indian goods and services in international markets
eligibility: Indian exporters, including MSMEs, engaged in export of goods or services, who have obtained an export order and require credit protection against buyer default. Banks lending to such exporters can also avail guarantees to secure their export credit exposure.
benefits: Protection against commercial and political risks, improved access to bank finance at better terms, enhanced creditworthiness of exporters, coverage for both pre-shipment and post-shipment risks, and support for export bill discounting and collection.
financial_support: ECGC provides credit guarantee covers typically up to 90% of the export value, reducing the risk for banks and enabling them to extend pre-shipment and post-shipment finance to exporters. Claims are settled upon buyer default due to insolvency, protracted default, or political events.
application_process: 1. Exporter or bank approaches ECGC with export contract details and buyer information. 2. Submit required documents including export order, invoice, and buyer creditworthiness details. 3. ECGC evaluates the risk and issues a credit guarantee policy. 4. Premium is paid based on risk assessment and coverage amount. 5. Policy is issued and can be used to secure bank finance. 6. In case of default, claim is filed with supporting documents for settlement.
required_documents: Bill of lading or airway bill
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications accepted throughout the year based on export transactions.
implementing_agency: Export Credit Guarantee Corporation of India Limited (ECGC), Ministry of Commerce and Industry
caveats: Coverage is subject to underwriting norms and country risk classifications
Claims are payable only after exhaustion of legal remedies and proof of default
Certain high-risk countries or buyers may be excluded or require higher premium
Policy must be obtained before shipment or extension of credit
Fraudulent claims or misrepresentation lead to rejection and legal action
